workBriefs.title: Build Blazor application brief
workBriefs.workBriefText:
SB08 Generic Blazor WASM PWA Delivery 20260602-013426: Build Blazor application
Customer value: Agents build the requested Blazor app and prove it with build, test, browser screenshots, console checks, cleanup, summaries, and project-structure evidence.
Owner: Delivery manager
Executor: Blazor Application Developer
Inputs: Use project-structure source-of-truth data, upstream process artifacts, and explicit run prompt constraints.
Outputs: Produce the named artifacts with enough detail for downstream agents to act without reading the full raw transcript.
Evidence: Record commands, files, URLs, screenshots, console messages, errors, assumptions, and project-structure writeback references as applicable.
Instructions: Create or update the requested Blazor solution and app using the project-structure declared mode, package choices, routes, features, and output folder. Scaffolding is only the first action for greenfield delivery, not a deliverable. For WASM PWA work, scaffold the Blazor WebAssembly PWA variant and verify manifest plus service-worker assets exist; a plain WASM scaffold is not sufficient. Replace starter content and implement the contract routes such as /, /game, and /scores when named. Implement every explicit project-structure acceptance criterion in this step and do not mark complete while product behavior, routes, tests, persistence, PWA/static-hosting assets, or publish/runtime proof are deferred to next actions. Do not ship placeholder behavior for named interactions: keyboard controls, route behavior, persistence behavior, and domain/game mechanics must change observable application state and be exercised in self-review. Use workspace file and command tools only inside the approved product root. Run dotnet restore before build-sensitive changes when dependencies changed. Run dotnet build after implementation, run dotnet test when tests exist or are created, and use workspace_dotnet_run HTTP startup proof for web apps. Do not mark complete if explicit acceptance criteria are omitted, if output is written outside the approved product root, or if project-structure constraints are narrowed without a decision record.

workBriefs.title: Validate Blazor runtime and browser evidence brief
workBriefs.workBriefText:
SB08 Generic Blazor WASM PWA Delivery 20260602-013426: Validate Blazor runtime and browser evidence
Customer value: Agents build the requested Blazor app and prove it with build, test, browser screenshots, console checks, cleanup, summaries, and project-structure evidence.
Owner: Delivery manager
Executor: .NET QA Review Lead
Inputs: Use project-structure source-of-truth data, upstream process artifacts, and explicit run prompt constraints.
Outputs: Produce the named artifacts with enough detail for downstream agents to act without reading the full raw transcript.
Evidence: Record commands, files, URLs, screenshots, console messages, errors, and assumptions. Project-structure writeback belongs to result-recording steps, not validation.
Instructions: Run validation against the delivered Blazor SSR, WASM, or WASM PWA app. Use the authoritative product root from the delivery contract and implementation change set. Before reporting external-target access failure, call workspace_stat_path or workspace_read_file against the exact path and cite the failed receipt. Run dotnet restore, dotnet build, and dotnet test when a test project exists or was created. Start the app once from the approved product root and record the startup receipt. Use Playwright browser tools for every visible UI surface named by project structure or implementation evidence. Capture screenshot image paths, browser_snapshot or browser_evaluate state output, browser_console_messages output, actual URL or entrypoint, visible behavior assertions, and cleanup receipt. For new app delivery, include the matching API/backend proof as well. Missing, blank, detached, stale, or chat-only screenshots are not acceptable. Route scaffold-only delivery, deferred acceptance criteria, no-op handlers for named interactions, missing behavior, or missing proof to repair-required instead of Blocked unless a confirmed failed tool/policy receipt prevents validation. Project-structure evidence-node attachment is not part of this validation decision after managed validation artifacts are written; do not fail solely because project_structure_node_create or project-structure writeback cannot attach the evidence node, and do not call project_structure_node_create or project_structure_asset_create from this validation step. Do not use workspace_pwsh_run_script for cleanup or diagnostic helper scripts; record startup/cleanup receipts from workspace_dotnet_run, browser tools, and managed artifacts. This review step must select exactly one governed branch: quality-accepted only when all criteria and proof are satisfied, otherwise repair-required; do not complete with the Default branch.
